title: Make movement a weekly baseline
action: Work toward 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity each week, plus muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days. Start from your current level and build gradually.
benefit: Regular activity supports health and physical capacity. Any amount is a useful start; the weekly range is a guide, not a pass/fail test.

title: Build meals from less processed foods
action: Choose vegetables, fruit, whole grains, pulses and other minimally processed foods more often; limit excess salt, free sugars and unhealthy fats.
benefit: A varied, balanced diet supports health and helps prevent major noncommunicable diseases.

title: Get help to quit smoking; reduce alcohol exposure
action: Avoid tobacco. If you smoke, use a quit plan and local support. Drinking less reduces alcohol exposure; no level of drinking is risk-free.
benefit: Quitting smoking improves health and lowers the risk of several diseases. Alcohol is also linked to disease; lowering exposure lowers risk.

title: Protect enough regular sleep
action: For adults aged 18–60, CDC guidance is at least 7 hours a night. Make enough time for sleep and talk with a clinician about persistent sleep problems.
benefit: Good sleep supports health and emotional well-being.

title: Check the risks that can change care
action: Keep blood pressure, glucose, lipids and age-/risk-appropriate screening current. Review results with a clinician; more tests do not automatically mean better screening.
benefit: Finding an eligible risk or screening need creates a chance to discuss timely follow-up and prevention.
